questions.question: When and why was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) adopted?
options: In 1948, by the UN, after the devastation of World War II
In 1989, after the fall of the Berlin Wall
questions.explanation: The UN adopted the UDHR in 1948 as a response to the atrocities of World War II.

questions.question: How many articles does the UDHR contain?
questions.explanation: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights consists of 30 articles describing fundamental rights for all people.

questions.question: What did the American Civil Rights Movement primarily fight against?
questions.explanation: The Civil Rights Movement fought racial segregation and discrimination against Black Americans, especially in the 1950s and 60s.

questions.question: What was the anti-apartheid movement about?
options: Ending the system of racial segregation in South Africa
Voting rights for women in Britain
questions.explanation: The anti-apartheid movement fought to end South Africa's system of legalised racial segregation.

questions.question: Which of these are contemporary social justice issues discussed in English-speaking media?
options: Racial equality, gender equality, LGBTQ+ rights and refugee rights
questions.explanation: Contemporary issues include racial and gender equality, LGBTQ+ rights, refugee and migration rights, and digital privacy.
